question: Why does the phone lose k2 to Withered Foxy (7 of 10 counted runs) while the model wins every seed, and do the model's Foxy errors touch encounter predictions?

dumpFacts.source: Office frame (FRAME 3) of the retained event dump; object identities confirmed against the Chowdren recompile's generated names (oldfoxy_105, indanger_125, viewinghalllight_127, mask_89, viewing_55, night_108, oldfoxyai_112, beingattackedby_136). The CTFAK dump's object NAMES are shifted; its OI numbers are right.

chain.g337: every 5000 ms, no location/pin/state condition: (21 + Random(5)) - D <= Foxy AI (cap 17, g829); success writes A=1 and D=0. The Random draw is spent every 5 s.
chain.g364: B > 0 -> B decays one per frame
chain.g389: A=2, at CAM 08, latch 0 -> hall (A=0, D=0)
chain.g390: A=2, in the hall, latch 0 -> marker 123 (the lock, A=0)
chain.g488/g489: latch cleared every 1000 ms, then set from lit? (viewing 0, power > 0)
chain.g571/g572: every 10000 ms, at 123, not being attacked, in danger 0 -> attack (either viewing state)
chain.g573: at 123, viewing 0, latch 1, in danger 0 -> attack
chain.g745: in the hall with the latch -> D=0, exposure += 1
chain.g825: in danger 0, mask fully on, nobody at 122, every 1000 ms -> D += 1
chain.g846: exposure > 100 x night, lit? 0, latch 0, B 0 -> CAM 08, A=0, D=0, exposure 0, B = 500 + Random(500); no position condition
chain.g855: in the hall with the latch -> B = 50
chain.g864: every 500 ms, D > 0, at CAM 08, latch 1 -> D -= 1
chain.startState: no night-start writer for Foxy's alterable values and empty object values: B starts at 0

timerOrder.claimLevel: SUPPORTING (Chowdren is a Fusion reimplementation, not the Android runtime)
timerOrder.reading: Chowdren generates each Every condition as an accumulator placed in condition order (`every += dt; if (every < T) skip; every -= T`, dt real elapsed time). g824 and g825 test in danger BEFORE their 1 s accumulator, so those timers pause during encounters and keep their remainder; g337, g864, g488, g571 and g572 put the timer first.
timerOrder.consequence: The model's D tick `(f + blackoutCount) % 60` and its mask-on accumulator that resets on mask-off are approximations of this; neither the per-encounter offset nor the reset is sourced.

modelGapsFound: The default model skips Foxy's roll, and its Random(5) draw, while he is pinned or not ready; g337 has no such gate.
The constructor draws Foxy's readyAt (5-10 s); the dump has no such draw, so every later draw is one step out of line.
A successful roll during the 50-frame pin is dropped by the model; the dump holds it in A and locks once B drains and the latch clears.
The model ticks D before the latch reset (the dump resets in g745 before g824 ticks).

encounterPredictionEffect.method: k2, Night 7, epoch 2433, seeds 1-3000, default model; variants add one draw at each 5 s Foxy roll the model skips, or remove only the constructor draw; office encounter sequence (who + frame) compared per seed
encounterPredictionEffect.reading: Rates are unchanged, but seed-specific predictions are not: with either fix the first encounter differs on ~78% of seeds and the 120 s sequence on >99%. Every seed-matched encounter prediction and seed-clock test scored on the default model ran on a stream out of step with g337, in addition to the g744 gap already recorded in docs/evidence/withered-freddy-route-night7-20260915.json.

deathCycleHallFlash.tool: cycle-ledger door region (640x288, rows 80:213, cols 240:453) at 60 fps, phase 7.16-7.76 s
deathCycleHallFlash.jumpscareOnset: door brightness rises to ~12-13 at ~7.70-7.73 s video phase in all seven, lit or not
deathCycleHallFlash.reading: The kill's visible onset does not wait on the flash; with ~160 ms capture latency (flash press 7.46 -> peak ~7.62) it sits nearer g571's 10 s attack at 7.567 s than the flash latch at ~7.48 s. Not resolved at this frame rate.

camdropHallRead.status: CALIBRATED by eyehole label; latch not observable
camdropHallRead.method: median door brightness 1.70-1.80 s video phase after each camdrop (cycle-ledger door region, 60 fps)

levels.~15.3: plain office, no hall light (the ledger's normal office ~16)

camdropHallRead.reading: Four of five timed death cycles show no camdrop hall light, against ~40% of other encounter-free cycles (~9% by chance). The render races the light's release 33 ms after the monitor finishes lowering, so an unlit render does not prove a missing latch; matching the phone's 3/10 needs ~9% of camdrops to fail to latch.

postMaskFlashLoss.reading: No undefended 7.46 s flash reads FLAT across the cohort, so a ~20% lost hall contact is not what the phone shows; the death-cycle 'no peak' reads are a DIM peak (r10) and one-frame dips (r07b, r09), not missing flashes.

conclusions: With lit? as the dump's persistent counter, the literal Foxy chain wins every seed on k2, k3 and Night 6 h: the earlier 2999/3000 was a model error (the drop-frame latch), not a phone mechanism.

The model now has no Foxy death path without an actuation failure; the phone's k2 deaths (encounter-free cycles, kill ~7.5 s) need Foxy locked at the 2.567 s roll, i.e. a camdrop whose light did not latch.
A lost 33 ms hall flash is not supported by the phone (0/107 FLAT on undefended cycles).
The Foxy draw errors scramble seed-specific encounter predictions (not rates).
openQuestions: Why ~9% of camdrops would fail to latch on the phone: the camera light touch not surviving the monitor tap (Multiple Touch pointer handling), or delivery order of the light and monitor contacts; not in the model and not yet observed directly.
A device observable for the drop-frame latch itself (the render cannot show it).
Whether a fresh hall contact after the drop and before the mask (1.35-1.70 s) removes the Foxy deaths: the model cannot rank it (k2 already wins 3000/3000 there).

litCounterFix.claimLevel: dump-sourced mechanic (Chowdren real names, Office events 74-83/211/382-384/425-426); censuses MODEL_ONLY

sourceFacts.lit: lit_75 is a persistent counter: held light sets it with viewing 0 and the mask off (74), on any camera but 10 (75) or on CAM 10 (76); release (79), battery 0 (80), in danger (81), the mask reaching fully on (82) and Balloon Boy inside (83) clear it
sourceFacts.drop: event 211 (the drop) sets viewing_55 = 0 in the same frame, after 74-83 and before in danger rises (382-384)
sourceFacts.latch: event 425 clears viewinghalllight_127 every 1 s; event 426 sets it with viewing 0, battery > 0 and lit 1 -- no in-danger condition
sourceFacts.consequence: a camera light held through the drop latches the hall on the drop frame even when an office encounter starts on that frame, so D resets and the 2.567 s roll cannot lock Foxy

androidRuntime.CND_EVERY2.eva2: first evaluation loads the delay into the parameter and returns false; later evaluations subtract CRun.rhTimerDelta and fire (adding the delay back) at <= 0 -- a countdown that moves only when the condition is reached, keeping its remainder
androidRuntime.rhTimerDelta: CRun.f_GameLoop: System.currentTimeMillis() difference per loop (real milliseconds)

litCounterFix.modelChange: sourcedFoxyChain now keeps lit? as that counter at frame start (updateLitCounter) and latches with viewing 0 and battery read after the drop; test pins the drop-frame latch under a starting encounter
litCounterFix.lostHallContactMethod: the 7.40-7.55 s light press dropped with probability P by a separate PRNG (the game RNG untouched)
